synthesis.body: web/src/content/journeys/ is part hand-maintained, part generated: tools/build-site.py regenerates 11 of the 17 files from packs/<pack>/JOURNEY.md. A fix applied only to the web/ copy survives until the next build-site.py run, then silently reverts. Before editing any file under a directory a generator writes into, check whether that specific file has an upstream source; the directory being partly hand-maintained is not evidence that the file you are editing is. Second trap, same directory: one generated file (journeys/product-documentation.md) is listed in a local .gitignore, so `git status` counted 37 changed files when 38 values were edited, and no git-status-based check can ever observe it reverting - assert its content directly. Reconcile the count of values you intended to change against git status and explain any gap before believing a sweep is complete. Caveat on attribution: do NOT assume a revert was caused by the projection just because a projection exists. When the same docsUrl fix was undone (PR#852 -> PR#854), the projection explained at most 11 of the 37 reverted files - the other 26 are never generated - and a stale base was disproved outright (git merge-base --is-ancestor showed #852 already in #854's ancestry). Verify the mechanism against the commit graph before writing it down; a plausible mechanism that is present is not the mechanism that fired.

title: A partly-generated content directory hides two traps: a projected file reverts, a gitignored one absorbs the edit
